cells.tense: Something you carried through a change is steady now, and it holds here where you work.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: Take what comes to you for the work, and give yours back at the size it truly is. No shrugging it off, no doubling it. That's the whole of it.
cells.core:
What you chose to keep through that change has settled into a shape you can use, and you can feel who fed this work and who leaned on it without either count coming out wrong. That kind of clear sight is rare in quiet work. It is what makes the calm worth keeping — not stillness for its own sake, but a level floor with a fair measure under it, so the practice holds you up and holds your people honestly too.

Let that measure run both directions. Take what is offered during your next stretch, and when you give, give it for real and let it end there. Then return to your bench. The work stays warm when you are neither paying for it nor carrying the whole of it.
cells.sheetLine: What you held through the change is steady enough to share.

cells.tense: The next version of this work has already arrived, and it pulls at you from outside too.
cells.act: hold the cloud of possible feeling without picking yet
cells.ask: Watch what draws your eye — a style, a direction, a way someone else does it — and pick nothing. Keep the sessions you have while it stays open. Let it pull without an answer.
cells.core:
Where you practise, the next form of the thing keeps arriving early. You can see where the work could go, who it could reach, what it could become, and you are already out there in it while today's repetition is still under your hands. Then the same something reaches toward other people: who took to it, who has not answered, what a small version taught somewhere might look like. None of that is a false move. The plan has just grown past the bench it grew up on.

So hold it open without answering. Keep the sessions you already have, let the next form stay only possible, and let the pull act on you. The draw settles into the work instead of leaning on it. You keep the reach and lose the lean.
cells.sheetLine: The plan has grown past the bench it grew from.

cells.tense: There was a door out of the old form, and you are still standing behind it.
cells.act: refuse the pull off course, once more
cells.ask: Let the next suggestion about your practice pass without acting on it. Hear it out, stay where you are, and see what the heading feels like before you say anything back.
cells.core:
The change already happened. What it cleared sits behind you somewhere, and the practice that came out of it has gone flat: hands moving through hours, nothing any of it is for in view. The shape is here, faithful and worn smooth, without the reason it was chosen. You may have let other voices decide too much of it, or you may simply have arrived late to your own work.

Make a direction in the practice and stand in it once. When the next suggestion comes — a new method, a should, someone else's way — let it pass without acting, and feel where that leaves the heading. That is not stubbornness and it needs no speech. Doing it once will show you what there was to keep.
cells.sheetLine: The shape is here. Its reason is still behind you.

cells.tense: The work continues, steady and unclaimed, in the hours you keep for it.
cells.act: make the call and carry it through
cells.ask: Make one call about the practice — a time, a piece you'll bring to the next session — and carry it. When someone asks what it's for, keep the reasons to yourself. Then stop.
cells.core:
There is something in your practice that steadies whatever comes across the desk and settles the week around it, and in your own account it gets called keeping busy. The steadying is real. What is missing is your voice claiming it. Other people see a clean surface, so they come and put things down on it, and when they ask what the practice is for you have a reply that sends them a step or two away and leaves the thing untouched.

No speech is required. Make one call and carry it — a time, a piece for the next session — and skip the explaining. One week of that and the authority already at work under your hands will be plain enough, at least to you.
cells.sheetLine: What gets called keeping busy is steadying the whole week.
